content: Refresh tokens (Microsoft Learn, updated 2026-06-15). Default lifetime 90 days for all scenarios except single-page apps and email OTP (24h). Refresh tokens REPLACE THEMSELVES on every use; the identity platform does NOT revoke the old one, so the client must persist the new refresh_token from each response and delete the old one. Revocation matrix: for public-client password-based tokens, a user password change / SSPR / admin password reset revokes; non-password (e.g. FIDO/Windows Hello) tokens survive password changes; user or admin revoking all refresh tokens revokes everything. Relevant AADSTS codes verified in the official error reference: AADSTS70008 ExpiredOrRevokedGrant (refresh token expired due to inactivity); AADSTS700082 ExpiredOrRevokedGrantInactiveToken (same, with issueDate/inactive duration - 'expected part of the token lifecycle'); AADSTS50173 grant expired due to revocation/password change, fresh auth needed; AADSTS53003 BlockedByConditionalAccess; AADSTS530035 BlockedBySecurityDefaults; AADSTS50076 UserStrongAuthClientAuthNRequired (MFA required); AADSTS50079 MFA enrollment required; AADSTS65001 DelegationDoesNotExist (user/admin has not consented); AADSTS90094 AdminConsentRequired; AADSTS7000112 application disabled; AADSTS500011 resource principal not found in tenant; AADSTS50194 app not configured as multitenant, /common unsupported for such apps created after a cutoff date; AADSTS700016 application not found in directory/tenant; AADSTS90002 InvalidTenantName; AADSTS50020 user account from identity provider does not exist in tenant. All of these surface under the top-level OAuth error name invalid_grant or invalid_client with the AADSTS code inside error_description.
